concepts.name: Reading a ratio
concepts.description: A ratio compares quantities in parts, not in absolute amounts.

concepts.name: Equivalent ratios
concepts.description: Scaling both terms by the same factor leaves a ratio unchanged.

concepts.name: Dividing in a given ratio
concepts.description: Splitting a total into parts that follow a ratio.

concepts.name: Proportion
concepts.description: Two equal ratios, and the cross-multiplication that follows.

concepts.name: Chained ratios
concepts.description: Combining A:B and B:C into A:B:C by matching the common term.

concepts.name: Ratio word problems
concepts.description: Turning statements about shares, mixtures and changes into ratio equations.

formulas.title: Share of a total
formulas.prompt: A total is divided in the ratio a : b. How do you find each share?
formulas.formula:
First share = Total × a/(a + b)
Second share = Total × b/(a + b)
formulas.explanation: Add the ratio terms to get the number of parts, find the value of one part, then scale.
formulas.example:
₹1,200 in 2 : 3
Parts = 5, one part = ₹240
Shares = ₹480 and ₹720
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying by a/b instead of a/(a+b) — that compares the shares rather than splitting the total.
formulas.applicationPrompt: ₹4,500 is shared between A and B in 4 : 5. Which expression gives A's share?

formulas.title: Value of one part
formulas.prompt: What is the fastest first step in almost every ratio question?
formulas.formula: One part = Total ÷ (sum of ratio terms)
formulas.explanation: Almost every ratio problem becomes arithmetic once you know what a single part is worth.
formulas.example:
91 divided in 4 : 3
Parts = 7, one part = 13
Shares = 52 and 39
formulas.commonMistake: Dividing by the number of terms (2) instead of the sum of the terms.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A total of 91 is split in 4 : 3. What is one part worth?

formulas.title: Proportion and cross multiplication
formulas.prompt: What does a : b = c : d let you write?
formulas.formula: a : b = c : d  ⟹  a × d = b × c
formulas.explanation: Equal ratios mean equal fractions, so cross multiplying gives a usable equation.
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying a × c and b × d, which pairs the wrong terms.
formulas.applicationPrompt: You are told 5 : 8 = x : 24. Which equation follows?

formulas.title: Fourth proportional
formulas.prompt: How do you find the fourth proportional to a, b and c?
formulas.explanation: It is cross multiplication rearranged: from a : b = c : x you get x = bc/a.
formulas.commonMistake: Mixing up the order of a, b and c — write the proportion out before substituting.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the fourth proportional to 4, 6 and 14.

formulas.title: Combining A : B and B : C
formulas.prompt: You know A : B and B : C. How do you get A : B : C?
formulas.formula: Scale both ratios so the B terms match, then read off A : B : C
formulas.explanation: Multiply the first ratio by B's value in the second, and the second by B's value in the first.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing 2 : 3 : 5 by just joining the ratios — the two B values must be made equal first.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5. What is A : B : C?

formulas.title: Compound ratio
formulas.prompt: What is the compound ratio of a : b and c : d?
formulas.explanation: Compounding multiplies corresponding terms — useful when two ratios act together, such as speed and time.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the terms instead of multiplying them.
formulas.applicationPrompt: What is the compound ratio of 2 : 3 and 4 : 5?

formulas.title: One part from the difference
formulas.prompt: Two quantities are in the ratio a : b and you know their difference, not their total. How do you find them?
formulas.explanation: The quantities differ by a − b parts, so the given difference is that many parts.
formulas.example: Ratio 7 : 4, difference 36: one part = 36 ÷ 3 = 12, so the quantities are 84 and 48.
formulas.commonMistake: Dividing the difference by a + b, as if it were the total.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Two numbers are in the ratio 9 : 5 and differ by 48.

formulas.title: Joining A : B and B : C in one line
formulas.prompt: A : B = a : b and B : C = c : d. What is A : B : C?
formulas.formula: A : B : C = ac : bc : bd
formulas.explanation: Multiply the first ratio by c and the second by b so the B terms both become bc.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing 2 : 3 : 5 by dropping the mismatched B terms.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7. Find A : C.

formulas.title: When aA = bB = cC
formulas.prompt: aA = bB = cC. What is A : B : C?
formulas.formula: A : B : C = 1/a : 1/b : 1/c = bc : ac : ab
formulas.explanation: Equal products mean each quantity is inversely proportional to its multiplier.
formulas.commonMistake: Writing the ratio as 2 : 3 : 4, the multipliers themselves.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 4 times A's share equals 5 times B's share and 10 times C's share.

formulas.title: Componendo and dividendo
formulas.prompt: An equation has the form (x + k)/(x − k) = p/q. What is the quickest way to x?
formulas.formula: If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d)
formulas.explanation: Adding and subtracting numerator and denominator on both sides keeps the equality and removes the sum-over-difference form.
formulas.commonMistake: Applying it to one side only.

levels.title: What a Ratio Actually Says
levels.description: Ratios describe parts, not amounts. Getting this straight prevents most errors.

blocks.title: A ratio is a comparison in parts
blocks.body:
When a recipe says flour and sugar are in the ratio 3 : 2, it is not saying 3 grams and 2 grams. It says: split whatever you have into 5 equal parts, give 3 to flour and 2 to sugar.

That is the whole idea. A ratio fixes the proportions but leaves the size open.

blocks.title: The move that solves most questions
blocks.body: One part = Total ÷ (sum of the ratio terms)
blocks.caption: Find what one part is worth, and the rest is multiplication.

blocks.body: Ratios are unchanged by scaling: 3 : 2, 6 : 4 and 30 : 20 are the same ratio. Always simplify before working — smaller numbers mean fewer mistakes.

blocks.title: Ratio vs fraction
blocks.body:
In the ratio 2 : 3, the first quantity is 2/5 of the total, not 2/3 of it. The 2/3 comparison answers a different question: how the first compares with the second.

Confusing these two is the single most common error in this topic.

levels.title: The Ratio Toolkit
levels.description: Recall the six relationships that cover almost every ratio question.

levels.title: Choose the Right Move
levels.description: Identify what a ratio question is really asking before you calculate.

levels.title: Direct Ratio Questions
levels.description: Simplifying, scaling and splitting totals — one step each.

levels.title: Sharing, Chaining and Proportion
levels.description: Three-way splits, chained ratios and proportion equations.

levels.title: Multi-Step Ratio Problems
levels.description: Word problems where the ratio has to be built before it can be used.

questions.question: Write the ratio 45 : 60 in its simplest form.
questions.explanation: Divide both terms by their HCF, 15: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 and 60 ÷ 15 = 4.
solutionSteps: Find the HCF of 45 and 60, which is 15.
questions.method: Divide both terms by their highest common factor.

hints.text: What is the largest number that divides both 45 and 60?
Both are divisible by 15.

commonMistakes: Stopping at 9 : 12, which is equivalent but not fully simplified.

questions.question: Two quantities are in the ratio 2 : 3. What fraction of the total is the first quantity?
questions.explanation: The total is 2 + 3 = 5 parts, and the first quantity is 2 of them, so 2/5.
solutionSteps: Add the ratio terms to get the number of parts: 2 + 3 = 5.
The first quantity takes 2 of those 5 parts.

hints.text: How many equal parts is the total split into?
2/3 compares the first with the SECOND, not with the total.

commonMistakes: Answering 2/3 by comparing the two quantities rather than using the total.

questions.question: ₹1,200 is divided between two people in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does the second person get?
questions.explanation: Five parts in total, so one part is ₹240. The second person gets 3 × 240 = ₹720.

hints.text: How many parts is ₹1,200 being split into?
One part = 1200 ÷ 5.

questions.question: 91 is divided in the ratio 4 : 3. What is the larger part?
questions.explanation: Seven parts in total, so one part is 13. The larger part is 4 × 13 = 52.

hints.text: 91 splits neatly into 7 parts.
One part = 13.

commonMistakes: Answering 39, which is the smaller part.

questions.question: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b = 20, what is a?
questions.explanation: b corresponds to 4 parts, so one part is 5 and a = 3 × 5 = 15.
questions.method: Find the value of one part from the known term.

hints.text: Which ratio term does b correspond to?
4 parts = 20, so 1 part = 5.

commonMistakes: Computing 3/4 of 20 correctly as 15 but then doubting it — check by forming 15 : 20 = 3 : 4 ✓

questions.question: ₹4,500 is shared between A and B in the ratio 4 : 5. Which expression gives A's share?
questions.explanation: There are 4 + 5 = 9 parts and A takes 4 of them, so A gets 4500 × 4/9 = ₹2,000.
questions.method: Share = Total × (own term ÷ sum of terms).

hints.text: The denominator should be the total number of parts.
4 : 5 means 9 parts altogether.

commonMistakes: Using 4/5, which compares A with B rather than with the total.

questions.question: You are told A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, and you need A : B : C. What must you do first?

options.text: Make B the same number in both ratios

questions.explanation: B appears as 3 in one ratio and 4 in the other. Scaling to a common value of 12 gives A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.
solutionSteps: B is 3 in the first ratio and 4 in the second.
Scale the first by 4 and the second by 3 so B becomes 12 in both.
questions.method: Match the common term before joining the ratios.

hints.text: B has two different values. Can both be true at once?
Find a common multiple of 3 and 4.

commonMistakes: Writing 2 : 3 : 5 by simply appending C's term.

questions.question: Adding 2 to both terms of the ratio 3 : 5 makes the ratio larger.
questions.explanation: 3/5 = 0.6 while 5/7 ≈ 0.714. Adding the same amount to both terms of a ratio below 1 moves it towards 1, so it increases.
questions.method: Convert both ratios to decimals and compare.

hints.text: Write each ratio as a fraction and compare their values.
Adding equally to both terms always pulls a ratio towards 1 : 1.

commonMistakes: Assuming adding the same value to both terms leaves the ratio unchanged — only multiplying does that.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanation: Make B equal in both: multiply the first ratio by 4 and the second by 3, giving 8 : 12 and 12 : 15.
questions.method: Scale both ratios to a common value of the shared term.

hints.text: B must have the same value in both ratios.
The LCM of 3 and 4 is 12.

commonMistakes: Joining the ratios without matching B.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. If 6 is added to each, the ratio becomes 7 : 9. What are the numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 5x and 7x. Then (5x + 6)/(7x + 6) = 7/9 gives 45x + 54 = 49x + 42, so x = 3 and the numbers are 15 and 21.
solutionSteps: 4x = 12, so x = 3 → the numbers are 15 and 21.
questions.method: Introduce x for one part, form a proportion, cross multiply.

hints.text: Write the numbers as 5x and 7x so the ratio is built in.
Form the equation (5x + 6)/(7x + 6) = 7/9.
Cross multiply and solve for x.

commonMistakes: Adding 6 to only one of the numbers.

questions.question: ₹6,000 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much does C receive?
questions.explanation: Twelve parts in total, so one part is ₹500. C gets 5 × 500 = ₹2,500.
questions.method: Same one-part method, extended to three terms.

hints.text: Add all three terms to find the number of parts.
One part = 6000 ÷ 12.

commonMistakes: Dividing by 3 (the number of people) instead of 12 (the number of parts).

questions.question: Find the fourth proportional to 4, 6 and 14.

hints.text: Set it up as 4 : 6 = 14 : x.
Cross multiply and solve for x.

commonMistakes: Pairing the numbers in the wrong order, giving 9.33.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 63 and they are in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the difference between them?
questions.explanation: Nine parts total, so one part is 7. The numbers are 28 and 35, and their difference is one part — 7.
questions.method: The difference between the terms is always (difference of ratio terms) × one part.

hints.text: Find the value of one part first.
The difference of the ratio terms is 5 − 4 = 1 part.

commonMistakes: Computing both numbers correctly and then subtracting incorrectly.

questions.question: In a mixture, milk and water are in the ratio 5 : 3. When 16 litres of water is added, the ratio becomes 5 : 7. How much milk is in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Let milk = 5x and water = 3x. Then 5x/(3x + 16) = 5/7 gives 35x = 15x + 80, so x = 4 and milk = 20 litres.
solutionSteps: Milk = 5 × 4 = 20 litres. Check: water becomes 12 + 16 = 28, and 20 : 28 = 5 : 7 ✓
questions.method: Hold the unchanged quantity fixed and let the ratio equation do the work.

hints.text: Only the water changes — the milk stays the same.
Write milk = 5x, water = 3x, then form the new ratio.

questions.question: ₹5,000 is divided among A, B and C so that A gets twice what B gets, and B gets three times what C gets. How much does A receive? (Answer in ₹)
questions.explanation: Let C = x. Then B = 3x and A = 6x, so 10x = 5,000, x = 500 and A = ₹3,000.
questions.method: Anchor on the smallest quantity, then express the others in terms of it.

hints.text: Start from C, since everything is defined relative to it.
If C = x, then B = 3x and A = 6x.
The ratio A : B : C is 6 : 3 : 1.

commonMistakes: Starting from A, which forces fractions unnecessarily.
